key_insight: EVENET learns reusable patterns from simulated particle collisions and transfers them to multiple analysis tasks. It also works on real collider data, bridging simulation-based training and experimental use.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis involves many specialized tasks. EVENET addresses the need for a shared model that can support different analyses and transfer knowledge from simulations to real measurements.
method: Pretrain a foundation model on simulated particle collision data.
Combine self-supervised learning with supervision from physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model across analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET demonstrates how foundation models can support scientific data analysis beyond language and images. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights the potential of combining self-supervision, domain labels, and simulation-based pretraining to build reusable models.
visual_elements: Training pipeline: simulated collisions → self-supervision + physics labels → EVENET.

paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
